statement_record.book: A preorder (P, ≤) determines a category P with Ob(P) = P and exactly one morphism p → q when p ≤ q, none otherwise; reflexivity gives identities and transitivity gives composition, and the category axioms hold automatically because hom-sets are subsingletons. Conversely a preorder is exactly a category in which any two parallel morphisms are equal.
statement_record.intree: Proset P : Category with obj := A, hom := R, homset := the trivial setoid (equiv := fun _ _ => True), id := reflexivity, compose := transitivity.
statement_record.strength_comparison: same. The setoid rephrasing is exactly the book's 'exactly one morphism when p ≤ q': hom p q is the (possibly proof-relevant) type R p q, and the trivial hom-setoid identifies all its inhabitants, so each hom-set is a subsingleton up to ≈ and every diagram commutes — the unitality/associativity obligations are discharged by that alone, as in the book. Not in-tree: the Hasse-diagram-as-presentation reading (a graph with ALL parallel paths declared equal — see the ABSENT record for 7sketches:3.2.3:ex3.21), and the fully assembled converse category ⟹ THIN CATEGORY (the preorder reflection AS a category); the converse at the level of the object preorder does exist, as hom_preorder (Theory/Category.v:282) - see the PARTIAL record for 7sketches:3.2.3:construction-preorder-reflection, which this verification pass overturned from ABSENT. Enriched_Two_preorder supplies the 'exactly' in the enriched formulation (2-enriched categories ↔ preorders, both directions) but not for a bare `Category`.

statement_record.book: From any category C one obtains a preorder (C, <=): take the underlying set C := Ob(C) and declare c1 <= c2 iff C(c1,c2) is nonempty. Reflexivity comes from identities and transitivity from composition. The reflection is blind to HOW MANY morphisms c1 -> c2 there are (one, two, fifty, infinitely many all give the same result), but does distinguish 'some morphism' from 'no morphism'.
statement_record.intree: hom_preorder {C : Category} : PreOrder (@hom C), with PreOrder_Reflexive := fun _ => id and PreOrder_Transitive := fun _ _ _ f g => g ∘ f - the objects of C carry a preorder whose relation is the hom itself, reflexive by identities and transitive by composition, exactly the book's two justifications.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: the preorder on objects is in-tree at Theory/Category.v:282 with precisely the book's witnesses (identities give reflexivity, composition gives transitivity), but the relation is the Type-valued hom ITSELF rather than the proposition 'C(c1,c2) is nonempty'. In a CRelationClasses setting with no propositional truncation, hom_preorder therefore retains the multiplicity of parallel morphisms - which is exactly the information the book's reflection is defined to destroy ('one, two, fifty, or infinitely many all give the same result'). statement_record.book: Free categories and preorders sit at opposite ends of one spectrum: from a graph, the free category imposes NO path equations (every path is a distinct morphism) while the preorder imposes ALL parallel-path equations. Every presentation (graph + equations) lies somewhere between the free category on that graph and its preorder reflection.
statement_record.intree: FreeOnQuiver G has hom := tlist edges (paths) with equivalence tlist_quiver_equiv, i.e. equality of paths — the free end, no equations. Quotient C R coarsens ≈ to any hom-congruence R, and HomCongruence's cong_incl field forces ≈ ⊆ R, i.e. every quotient lies above the free equivalence.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: the FREE end of the spectrum is fully present (paths of a quiver, distinct unless equal as paths), and the 'presentations are quotients above the free equivalence' half of the ordering is present as the cong_incl field of HomCongruence. The PREORDER end is missing AS THE TOP OF THE SPECTRUM: the object-level preorder of a category does exist (hom_preorder, Theory/Category.v:282 - reflexivity by id, transitivity by composition), but no congruence identifying all parallel morphisms is ever constructed, so the preorder reflection is never realized as a quotient of FreeOnQuiver G and cannot serve as the spectrum's upper bound. The 'lies between' claim is therefore only half-anchored, and is nowhere stated as a proposition.

statement_record.book: Set is the category whose objects are all sets, whose hom-set Set(S,T) is the set of functions S → T, whose identity id_S(s) = s, and whose composite (f;g)(s) := g(f(s)); unitality and associativity hold, so Set is a category.
statement_record.intree: Two realizations. Instance/Coq.v: obj := Type, hom A B := A → B, id := λ x, x, compose := λ g f x, g (f x), hom-equivalence pointwise Leibniz equality. Instance/Sets.v: obj := SetoidObject (a Type with an equivalence), hom := SetoidMorphism (a function plus a respectfulness proof), composition := ordinary function composition, hom-equivalence := pointwise ≈.
statement_record.strength_comparison: same. `Coq` is the literal transcription of Definition 3.24 (objects are types, morphisms honest functions, composition diagrammatic order after unfolding); `Sets` is the library's canonical Set — the target of every presheaf, hom-functor, Yoneda and end development — and its setoid rephrasing (hom-setoids and ≈ in place of =) is the sanctioned faithful encoding. Two disclosed foundational differences, neither a weakening of the book's claim: (i) `obj := Type@{o}` is universe-polymorphic, so 'the collection of ALL sets' is realized one universe at a time rather than as a proper class — the library's own note on the resulting size obstructions is in Instance/Sets.v and Instance/Sets/Classifier.v; (ii) function equality is pointwise, not Leibniz, so no funext is needed. Instance/Ens.v, despite its name and nLab pointers, is NOT this category: its morphisms are required to satisfy x ∈ A ↔ f x ∈ B, so it is not the category of sets and arbitrary functions.

evidence.intree_statement: Program Definition FinSet : Category := {| obj := nat; hom := fun m n => Fin.t m → Fin.t n; homset := fun m n => fun_setoid (Fin.t m) (Fin.t n); id := fun _ i => i; compose := fun _ _ _ f g i => f (g i) |}.

statement_record.book: FinSet is the category whose objects are the finite sets and whose morphisms are the functions between them, with identities and composition as in Set — i.e. the full subcategory of Set on the finite sets.
statement_record.intree: FinSet : Category with obj := nat (the object n standing for the canonical n-element set Fin.t n), hom m n := ALL functions Fin.t m → Fin.t n, identity the identity function, composition function composition, hom-setoid pointwise Leibniz equality.
statement_record.strength_comparison: same up to the standard skeletal presentation, with one disclosed difference: the in-tree FinSet is the SKELETON of the book's FinSet (objects are naturals, not finite sets), hence equivalent but not isomorphic to it. The morphism clause is exact — every function between the canonical finite sets is a morphism, no injectivity or other side condition — so the 'full subcategory' content is faithfully rendered. The library never builds the full subcategory of Sets on finite objects (Construction/Subcategory.v provides full subcategories generically, but is never instantiated at finiteness), and the equivalence between the skeleton and that subcategory is not proved in-tree; the file's own header states the skeletal choice explicitly ('The skeleton of the category of finite sets').

verifier.notes: Verified 'Program Definition FinSet : Category' at Instance/FinSet.v:116 with obj := nat, hom m n := Fin.t m -> Fin.t n (ALL functions, no side condition), homset := fun_setoid (pointwise Leibniz equality), id and compose the identity function and function composition - the quote is exact. The skeletal disclosure is the file's own (Instance/FinSet.v:17-19, 'The skeleton of the category of finite sets'), and skeleton-vs-full-subcategory is a presentational difference only (equivalent categories), so PRESENT is right under the frozen definition. Independently confirmed the classifier's supporting claim that Construction/Subcategory.v is never instantiated at finiteness: rg -ln 'Subcategory' --glob '*.v' returns Monad/Thunkable.v, Construction/Localization/Universal.v, Construction/Reflective.v, Theory/Lawvere/Model.v, Theory/Lawvere/Sets.v, Theory/Algebra/Comonoid/Hom.v, Structure/Binoidal/Central.v, Structure/Premonoidal/Freyd.v, Theory/Algebra/Monoid/Hom.v, Theory/Sheaf/Category.v - none about finite sets. evidence.intree_statement: Lemma fin_apply_tabulate {m n : nat} (f : Fin.t m → Fin.t n) (i : Fin.t m) : fin_apply (fin_tabulate f) i = f i.
Lemma fin_tabulate_apply {m n : nat} (c : Fin.t (n ^ m)) : fin_tabulate (fin_apply c) = c.
Program Instance FinSet_Closed : @Closed FinSet FinSet_Cartesian := { exponent_obj := fun m n => (n ^ m)%nat; exp_iso := fun x y z => {| to := ... fin_tabulate ...; from := ... fin_apply ... |} }.

statement_record.book: With 2 = {1,2} and 3 = {1,2,3} as objects of Set, list all elements of Set(2,3): there are nine (3^2) functions.
statement_record.intree: fin_tabulate : (Fin.t m → Fin.t n) → Fin.t (n ^ m) and fin_apply : Fin.t (n ^ m) → Fin.t m → Fin.t n are mutually inverse — fin_apply_tabulate pointwise (which is exactly FinSet's hom-equivalence) and fin_tabulate_apply on the nose — so the hom-set FinSet(m,n) is in bijection with the (n^m)-element set Fin.t (n^m); FinSet_Closed names n^m as the exponential object.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-stronger: the book's exercise is the single instance m = 2, n = 3, whereas the in-tree pair of round trips proves the general counting bijection FinSet(m,n) ≅ Fin.t (n^m) for all m, n, funext-free, and the codecs compute — Instance/FinSet/Closed.v:60/67 exercise them at exactly m = 2, n = 3, where n^m reduces to 9. Nothing in-tree tabulates the nine functions by name; that is a presentational rather than a mathematical difference, since fin_tabulate enumerates them positionally (the code k : Fin.t 9 IS the k-th function 2 → 3).

verifier.notes: All three evidence sites verified at the cited lines: fin_apply_tabulate (Instance/FinSet/Closed.v:79, pointwise, i.e. exactly FinSet's hom-setoid), fin_tabulate_apply (line 90, on the nose in Fin.t (n^m)), FinSet_Closed (line 132, exponent_obj := fun m n => (n ^ m)%nat, exp_iso built from fin_tabulate/fin_apply; the quote omits only the '#[export]' attribute). Together these are a genuine bijection FinSet(m,n) ≅ Fin.t (n^m) up to the hom-setoid, so |FinSet(2,3)| = |Fin.t 9| = 9 - the exercise's content, proved in general rather than at the single instance. The 'intree-stronger' comparison is honest and even understated: I independently confirmed that Instance/FinSet/Closed.v:60-70 exercises the codecs at LITERALLY m = 2, n = 3 (fin_tabulate_computes / fin_apply_computes, both by eq_refl, the code 2*3+1 = 7 lying in Fin.t 9). Nothing in-tree names the nine functions individually, which the record already discloses. PRESENT stands.

evidence.intree_statement: Theorem Category_is_Enriched_over_Set : Enriched Sets ↔ Category.  (* both directions Defined: a Sets-enriched category yields obj := eobj, hom := ehom, id := eid ttt, compose (f,g) := ecompose (f,g); conversely a Category yields Build_Enriched over Sets_Product_Monoidal with ehom x y := {| carrier := x ~> y |} *)

statement_record.book: V-categories are not categories with extra structure. Some V-categories (Bool-categories = preorders) can naturally be seen as categories, others (Cost-categories = Lawvere metric spaces) cannot. The precise relationship runs the other way: categories in the sense of Definition 3.6 are exactly Set-categories.
statement_record.intree: Category_is_Enriched_over_Set : Enriched Sets ↔ Category — an iffT, i.e. maps in both directions between Sets-enriched categories and ordinary Categories; Enriched_Two_preorder : Enriched _2 ↔ TwoPreorder for the truth-value base.
statement_record.strength_comparison: same for the remark's substantive claim (categories = Set-categories), and the Bool-category clause is likewise present, in both directions, over the walking arrow _2 with its cartesian monoidal structure. Two disclosed shortfalls, neither touching the claim's content: (i) `↔` here is iffT — the two constructions are exhibited and the file's header states the round trip is definitional, but no lemma asserts they are mutually inverse, so 'exactly' is witnessed by maps rather than by a proved bijection/equivalence (the morphism level is separately covered by Functor_is_Enriched_over_Set, Construction/Enriched.v:215, and the 2-cell level by EnrichedTransform_is_Transform, Construction/Enriched/Sets.v:49); (ii) the contrasting example — Cost-categories / Lawvere metric spaces — has no in-tree realization at all (rg -in 'metric space|Lawvere metric' over *.v returns PROSE only - Construction/Enriched.v:40/49/75, Construction/Karoubi.v:45/86, Theory/Profunctor.v:46/100 all describe Lawvere's ([0,∞], ≥, +)-enrichment in headers - and no Cost/quantale base or Cost-enriched instance is ever constructed), so the 'others cannot be seen as categories' half is illustrative prose with no counterpart.

evidence.intree_statement: Definition Opposite `(C : Category) : Category := {| obj := @obj C; hom := fun x y => @hom C y x; homset := fun x y => @homset C y x; id := @id C; compose := fun _ _ _ f g => g ∘ f; id_left := fun x y f => @id_right C y x f; id_right := fun x y f => @id_left C y x f; comp_assoc := fun x y z w f g h => @comp_assoc_sym C w z y x h g f; comp_assoc_sym := fun x y z w f g h => @comp_assoc C w z y x h g f |}.  (* Notation "C ^op" := (@Opposite C) *)

statement_record.book: For any category C, C^op has Ob(C^op) := Ob(C) and C^op(c,d) := C(d,c), with the identities and composition of C (composition with arguments swapped); C^op is again a category.
statement_record.intree: Opposite C : Category with obj := obj C, hom x y := hom C y x, homset x y := homset C y x, id := id C, compose f g := g ∘ f, and the unit/associativity laws taken from C's with left/right and assoc/assoc_sym interchanged.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-stronger: the definition is the book's on the nose (same objects, hom-sets swapped, same identities, composition with arguments exchanged, and the category laws established by permuting C's own fields), and the library additionally proves op_invol : (C^op)^op = C — Leibniz equality of categories, which the book does not state. The paired comp_assoc/comp_assoc_sym and id_left/id_right fields of Theory/Category.v exist precisely so that Opposite permutes fields rather than composing them with symmetry proofs; the construction is also extended in-tree to functors (Functor/Opposite.v), natural transformations (Natural/Transformation/Opposite.v) and isomorphisms (Isomorphism_Opposite, Construction/Opposite.v:146).

verifier.notes: Verified field by field against Construction/Opposite.v:106-121: obj := @obj C, hom x y := @hom C y x, homset x y := @homset C y x, id := @id C, compose f g := g ∘ f, id_left/id_right swapped, comp_assoc := comp_assoc_sym and vice versa - the quote is exact (compose_respects is re-bracketed as quoted). op_invol : (C^op)^op = C is at line 126 and is proved by unfold/destruct/f_equal, i.e. genuine Leibniz equality of categories, so 'intree-stronger' is honest. The claim that the paired laws of Theory/Category.v exist for this purpose is corroborated by Theory/Category.v itself (comp_assoc_sym is a field, not a derived lemma). Isomorphism_Opposite is at Construction/Opposite.v:146 as claimed. File registered in _CoqProject. PRESENT stands.
